source: Sri Lanka Department of Agriculture, FCRDI chilli crop guidance

entries.content: Sri Lankan chilli guidance identifies about 21 C to 27 C as a suitable temperature range and notes rain-fed production in areas receiving roughly 600 to 1000 mm annual rainfall.

When chilli plants wilt, first record whether one plant or a patch is affected, whether wilting is temporary or permanent, and whether the soil is dry, saturated, or poorly drained before suggesting a cause.
confirmation_questions: Is the soil dry or waterlogged near the roots?
Are single plants or a spreading patch affected?

entries.content: Sunken circular lesions on chilli fruit, sometimes developing darker concentric structures, require prompt inspection and expert confirmation because several fruit rots can appear similar.
Use clean planting material, remove diseased residues, maintain drainage and recommended spacing, and avoid moving contaminated soil between chilli fields.
actions: Clean tools before using them in another field

entries.content: For curled or distorted chilli leaves, inspect the tender shoots and leaf undersides for aphids, thrips, whiteflies, honeydew, or feeding scars before attributing the symptom to disease.
confirmation_questions: Are insects present beneath young leaves?
